subject: Shiny Server and HTTP status 304 (Not Modified)

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Shiny Server and HTTP status 304 (Not Modified)
parts:
I've been examining the HTTP headers of requests being made by the Chrome browser using the Live HTTP Headers Chrome extension.  I've also been looking at web server logs.  It appears that Shiny Server will almost never return a status 304 (Not Modified) even when the browser is re-requesting a static file that it has received before - e.g. jquery.min.js, bootstrap.min.css, shiny.min.js, etc.).  It's always a status 200.  The only exception seems to be a couple files under the "__assets__" directory, such as "__assets__/sockjs-0.3.4.min.js".

Is this the correct behavior for Shiny Server?  Is it possible I've done something in my particular configuration that thwarts caching?

Ideally, I'd like the browser to be able to cache these numerous static assets and not re-download them if they haven't changed, even across different Shiny apps.

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server and HTTP status 304 (Not Modified)
parts:
On Friday, June 3, 2016 at 2:00:21 AM UTC-4, Joel M. wrote:
I've been examining the HTTP headers of requests being made by the Chrome browser using the Live HTTP Headers Chrome extension.  I've also been looking at web server logs.  It appears that Shiny Server will almost never return a status 304 (Not Modified) even when the browser is re-requesting a static file that it has received before - e.g. jquery.min.js, bootstrap.min.css, shiny.min.js, etc.).  It's always a status 200.  The only exception seems to be a couple files under the "__assets__" directory, such as "__assets__/sockjs-0.3.4.min.js".

Is this the correct behavior for Shiny Server?  Is it possible I've done something in my particular configuration that thwarts caching?

Ideally, I'd like the browser to be able to cache these numerous static assets and not re-download them if they haven't changed, even across different Shiny apps.

So, one approach with which I've experimented is having nginx serve up the static files like shiny.min.js that would otherwise be served up by Shiny Server.  This appears to work since nginx will respond with a 304 (Not Modified) when the client re-requests the same static files.  This can be accomplished with an nginx configuration file similar to the one below.

One downside to this approach is that it requires always keeping the copies of the static files (under /static_assets/) in sync with those same files that would otherwise emanate from various Shiny-related R packages like Shiny and shinyBS (which are supported in the nginx.conf snippet below).

        location /static_assets/ {

            root  /srv/nginx;

            try_files  $uri  =404;

        }


        location ~ /(shiny_app1|shiny_app2|shiny_app3) {

            # This rewrite rule is to have static assets that would otherwise be served by a Shiny server, instead be served up by nginx, which supports caching via HTTP 304 responses.

            rewrite ^/(shiny_app1|shiny_app2|shiny_app3)/((shared|sbs)/[^\?].*)$  /static_assets/$2  last;
...
        }


Has anyone come up with other solutions for improving the caching behavior of Shiny applications?

Joel
